title: Flowgram Workflow Orchestration Overview
content:
Flowgram is a visual workflow orchestration engine that supports building complex business processes by dragging and dropping nodes.

## Core Concepts
- Node: The basic execution unit of a workflow; each node completes a type of task
- Edge: The connection between nodes, defining the execution order and data flow direction
- Variable Reference: Nodes pass data to each other via ${node_id.field} syntax
- Workflow: A directed acyclic graph (DAG) composed of nodes and edges

## Node Type Categories
- Flow Control: start, end, condition, multi-condition, branches, loop, break, continue
- Data Processing: variable, string-format, code
- Integration Calls: http, llm, workflow
- Human Participation: assignee
- Organizational Aids: comment, group, block-start, block-end

## Orchestration Principles
1. Every workflow must have exactly one start node
2. At least one end node to receive the final output
3. Data between nodes is passed via variable references
4. Complex logic should be split into multiple small nodes rather than a single large node
5. Loops and conditional branches should avoid infinite loops and unreachable paths

title: HTTP Node Usage Guide
content:
The HTTP node is used to initiate HTTP requests within a workflow to integrate external APIs.

## Configuration Fields
- method: HTTP method (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH)
- url: Request address, supports variable references, e.g. https://api.example.com/users/${start.input.userId}
- headers: Request header key-value pairs, commonly used for Authorization, Content-Type
- params: URL query parameters
- body: Request body (used with POST/PUT), can be a JSON string
- timeout: Timeout duration (milliseconds), default 30000

## Output
- status: HTTP status code (e.g. 200, 404, 500)
- response: Response body (parsed JSON object or string)
- headers: Response headers

## Common Usage
1. Call RESTful API to fetch data: GET https://api.example.com/users
2. Submit data: POST https://api.example.com/orders, body is the order JSON
3. Authentication: Add Authorization: Bearer ${start.input.token} to headers

## Notes
- It is recommended to set a reasonable timeout to prevent long blocking
- Pay attention to memory usage for large response bodies
- Error handling: Use a condition node to check status and decide the subsequent flow

title: LLM Node Configuration Guide
content:
The LLM node is used to call large language models and is the core of Agent workflows.

## Configuration Fields
- model: Model name (e.g. qwen/qwen3-4b-2507)
- apiHost: LLM service address (e.g. http://localhost:1234/v1)
- apiKey: API key
- temperature: Sampling temperature (0.0-2.0, 0 is most deterministic, 2 is most random)
- systemPrompt: System prompt, defines the model role and constraints
- userPrompt: User prompt, supports variable references
- maxTokens: Maximum number of generated tokens

## Output
- result: The text generated by the model
- usage: Token usage statistics (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens)

## Prompt Writing Tips
1. Clearly define the role and constraints in systemPrompt, e.g. "You are a data analysis assistant"
2. Provide specific tasks and context in userPrompt, using ${node.field} to reference upstream data
3. Complex tasks can be split into multiple LLM nodes connected in series
4. Require structured output (e.g. JSON) in the prompt for easier subsequent parsing

## Example
systemPrompt: You are a translation assistant, translate the user input into English
userPrompt: ${start.input.text}

## Notes
- High temperature is suitable for creative writing, low temperature is suitable for factual tasks
- Pay attention to token limits; long inputs need to be truncated or split
- Configure fallback logic when the API is unavailable

title: Conditional Branching: Condition vs Branches vs Multi-Condition
content:
Flowgram provides three conditional branch nodes for different scenarios.

## Condition Node (Single Condition)
- Applicable: Simple if-else binary choice
- Configuration: A single condition expression (left + operator + right)
- Output: Two branches: true / false
- operator: equal, not_equal, greater_than, less_than, greater_than_or_equal, less_than_or_equal, contains, not_contains, is_empty, is_not_empty, is_true, is_false

## Multi-Condition Node (Combined Conditions)
- Applicable: Complex combined condition judgment
- Configuration: Multiple sub-conditions combined via AND/OR
- Output: Multiple branches + default
- Suitable for: Nested conditions, multi-factor decisions

## Branches Node (Multi-way Branching)
- Applicable: Mutually exclusive multi-way branching, each branch has an independent sub-flow
- Configuration: One condition + sub-flow per branch
- Output: Independent path per branch + default
- Suitable for: Routing to different processing flows based on different types

## Selection Recommendations
- Use Condition for single condition judgment
- Use Multi-Condition for combined condition judgment
- Use Branches for multi-way independent sub-flows
- Note: Branches match in order and stop on hit

title: Loop Nodes: Loop with Break/Continue
content:
The Loop node is used to execute a sub-flow repeatedly, paired with Break/Continue to control the loop.

## Loop Types
- count: Fixed-count loop, configure count upper limit
- forEach: Iterate over a list, configure iterateOver list variable
- while: Conditional loop, configure condition termination condition

## Break Node
- Used to break out of a loop early
- Paired with Condition: break when condition is met
- Only breaks out of the nearest Loop

## Continue Node
- Skips the remaining logic of the current iteration
- Proceeds to the next iteration
- Paired with Condition

## Example: Iterate Over a User List for Processing
1. Loop (forEach, iterateOver: ${start.input.users})
2. Internal HTTP node calls the processing API
3. Condition checks the processing result
4. On failure, Continue to skip
5. Accumulate the success count and output via End

## Notes
- while loops must ensure the condition eventually becomes false, otherwise infinite loop
- Pay attention to performance and memory when iterating over large lists
- Nested loop Break only breaks out of the inner loop

title: Variable Reference Syntax Detailed Explanation
content:
Flowgram passes data between nodes via the ${node_id.field} syntax.

## Basic Syntax
- ${start.input.xxx}: Reference the input parameter of the Start node
- ${node_id.field}: Reference an output field of a certain node
- ${variable_node.var_name}: Reference a variable of a Variable node

## Supported Locations
- userPrompt, systemPrompt of the LLM node
- url, headers, params, body of the HTTP node
- left, right of the Condition node
- inputs of the Code node
- template of the String-Format node
- value of the Variable node
- outputs of the End node

## Nested References
- Supports object nesting: ${http_1.response.body.user.name}
- Supports array indexing: ${loop_1.items[0].id}

## Notes
- The referenced node must have been executed upstream
- Field names must match the node output schema
- Referencing an undefined variable will cause a runtime error
- Variable nodes are often used for intermediate variable relay

title: Code Node: Dynamic Code Execution
content:
The Code node is used to execute custom code, supporting Java, Groovy, and JavaScript.

## Configuration Fields
- language: Script language (java/groovy/javascript)
- code: Code content
- inputs: Input parameters (variable name + reference expression)
- outputs: Output parameters (variable name + type)

## Java Engine
- Dynamically compiled and executed, must comply with compilation specifications
- Class name is usually dynamically generated
- Receives upstream variables via inputs
- Returns results via return or outputs field

## Groovy Engine
- Script-style writing, more flexible
- Suitable for rapid logic implementation
- Performance is slightly lower than Java but development efficiency is higher

## JavaScript Engine
- Suitable for lightweight data processing
- Executed via JsFunExecNode

## Use Cases
1. Complex data transformation (JSON parsing, field extraction)
2. Algorithm computation (sorting, filtering, aggregation)
3. Business rule validation
4. String processing

## Notes
- Pay attention to code security, avoid executing untrusted code
- Complex logic is recommended to be split into multiple nodes
- Java code needs attention to class loading and memory

title: Variable and String-Format Nodes: Data Processing Tools
content:
Variable and String-Format are common nodes for data relay and formatting in workflows.

## Variable Node
- Purpose: Declare, assign, and modify variables
- Configuration: variables list (name, type, value)
- value supports variable references and expressions
- Output: Variables can be accessed in subsequent nodes via ${variable_node.var_name}
- Scenarios:
  - Intermediate variable relay
  - Data format conversion
  - Accumulator, counter
  - Default value fallback

## String-Format Node
- Purpose: Generate strings based on templates
- Configuration:
  - template: Template string, contains placeholders
  - engine: Template engine (thymeleaf/plain)
  - inputs: Variable bindings
- Output: formatted (the rendered string)
- Scenarios:
  - Prompt concatenation (combined with LLM node)
  - Email and report template rendering
  - URL concatenation
  - Multi-variable combined output

## Thymeleaf Syntax Example
template: Hello [[${user.name}]], your order [[${order.id}]] is [[${order.status}]]

## Plain Mode
template: Hello ${user.name}, your order ${order.id} is ${order.status}

## Selection Recommendations
- Use Variable for simple assignment
- Use String-Format for template rendering
- Use Code for complex logic

title: Sub-workflow Invocation: Workflow Node
content:
The Workflow node is used to invoke another defined workflow, enabling reuse and modularization.

## Configuration Fields
- workflowCode: Sub-workflow code
- version: Sub-workflow version (optional, defaults to latest)
- inputs: Input parameters passed to the sub-workflow
- outputs: Output fields returned by the sub-workflow

## Execution Flow
1. The parent workflow executes to the Workflow node
2. Starts the sub-workflow instance
3. Waits for the sub-workflow to complete
4. The outputs of the sub-workflow End node become the output of this node
5. The parent workflow continues execution

## Use Cases
- Common sub-flow reuse (e.g. user query, order validation)
- Modular splitting of complex workflows
- Team collaboration: different teams maintain different sub-workflows

## Notes
- Avoid circular references: A calls B, B cannot call A again
- Sub-workflow exceptions propagate to the parent workflow
- Pay attention to input/output parameter matching; extra or missing will cause errors
- Nesting depth should not be too deep, affects performance and debugging
- The start node inputs of the sub-workflow must match the inputs passed in by the parent workflow

title: Workflow Debugging and Best Practices
content:
Debugging tips and best practices in Flowgram workflow development.

## Debugging Tips
1. Single-node run: Use TestRun to execute a single node independently for validation
2. Variable inspection: Insert Variable nodes after key nodes to record intermediate state
3. Log output: Use Code nodes to print logs to assist troubleshooting
4. Segmented testing: Test the first half first, then gradually expand
5. Boundary testing: Test empty input, abnormal input, and oversized data

## Best Practices
1. Single responsibility: Each node does only one thing
2. Clear naming: Node title describes the function
3. Comment supplementation: Add Comment nodes for complex logic
4. Error handling: Add Condition after HTTP/LLM nodes to judge success
5. Variable conventions: Use meaningful variable names
6. Avoid deep nesting: Loops and condition nesting should not exceed 3 levels
7. Reuse first: Abstract common logic into sub-workflows

## Performance Optimization
- LLM nodes are the slowest, reduce unnecessary calls
- Pay attention to timeout settings for HTTP nodes
- Pay attention to batch processing for large list loops
- Code nodes should avoid recomputation

## Common Pitfalls
- Variable reference field name spelling errors
- Type mismatch in Condition (string vs number)
- Loop infinite loops
- Sub-workflow circular references
- End node outputs missing fields

title: Assignee Node: Human Task Integration
content:
The Assignee node is used to insert human task nodes into a workflow.

## Configuration Fields
- assignee: Handler (user ID or username)
- taskName: Task name
- taskDesc: Task description
- form: Form field schema filled in by humans
- timeout: Task timeout duration

## Execution Flow
1. The workflow pauses when it executes to the Assignee node
2. Creates a human task and notifies the assignee
3. Waits for the assignee to process and submit the form
4. The form data becomes the node output
5. The workflow continues execution

## Form Design
- Fields: name, type, required, default, options
- Types: text, number, select, textarea, date
- Example: The approval node form includes approved (boolean), comment (text)

## Use Cases
- Approval flows (leave, reimbursement, contract)
- Data entry (human-supplemented information)
- Decision confirmation (human-selected path)
- Exception handling (human intervention)

## Notes
- Requires external task system integration
- Pay attention to timeout handling strategies (auto-approve, auto-reject, escalation)
- Form field design should be concise and clear
- A handover mechanism is needed when the handler leaves

title: Block Nodes: Logical Block Organization
content:
Block-Start and Block-End nodes are used to organize logical blocks.

## Purpose
- Define code block / logical block boundaries
- Pair with Loop nodes to define loop bodies
- Pair with condition nodes to define condition blocks
- Improve readability

## Configuration
- Block-Start: blockId (block identifier)
- Block-End: blockId (must match the corresponding Block-Start)
- The two must appear in pairs

## Use Cases
1. Loop body: Block-Start ... loop content ... Block-End
2. Condition block: Clearly define the scope of the condition
3. Visual grouping of complex flows

## Notes
- Block-Start must have a corresponding Block-End
- Blocks cannot cross Loop/Condition boundaries
- Nested blocks must ensure blockId is unique
- Blocks do not affect execution logic, only used for organization
- Difference from Group node: Block is a logical boundary, Group is a visual grouping
